I watched most of it. He makes some good points but I think he's making one fatal assumption.

He's treating OOP as a design philosophy that must be rigidly followed at all times and almost all the "problems" and flaws he points out are if you just try to follow all the tenets of it perfectly in every situation.

Truth is, there is not one single design philosophy that is absolutely infallible and handles all situations perfectly. Trying to follow ANY abstract design philosophy too zealously will always lead to problems, because it either provides unnecessary limitations or you begin having to do extra unnecessary work to follow it for no other purpose than to follow it.

All these design philosophies should be viewed as guidelines you can use to help you think about what the best solution to your problem is. Don't worry so much about following some prepacked set of holy rules, but instead be aware of the guidelines and philosophies so you can tailor your solution to the problem. Follow proven guidelines where it makes sense, do alternative stuff if it makes sense, and don't feel like you are committing some major sin if you need to do so.
